subject.title: fix: prevent operational notices from leaking to source chats

question: Should OpenClaw accept a core `messages.operationalReplies` policy whose redirect mode fails closed when the operator-session write cannot be persisted, or require a different recovery contract before this feature proceeds?
rationale: The choice trades possible operational-notice loss against leaking potentially sensitive runtime details back into the originating chat; source inspection and tests cannot decide that security and operator-experience policy.

options.title: Approve fail-closed redirect
options.body: Keep source suppression on redirect-write failure, require a documented recovery path and current-head installed-channel proof before merge.

options.title: Design a recoverable redirect contract
options.body: Specify retry, durable queue, or another operator-visible recovery mechanism before accepting the new redirect behavior.

options.title: Defer the core policy
options.body: Keep the linked policy discussion open and do not merge this broad config and persisted-state surface until a maintainer sponsors its direction.

recommendation.title: Approve fail-closed redirect
recommendation.body: Keep source suppression on redirect-write failure, require a documented recovery path and current-head installed-channel proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor authored the current implementation and the linked policy proposal, so they are the clearest available routing contact for the requested decision packet.
